how_to_run: For each eval, run the prompt with-skill and baseline (no skill) in fresh sessions, in parallel. Fresh means uncontaminated: run from a directory outside any CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md tree, e.g. `claude -p --setting-sources "" --add-dir <skill dir>` with the prompt on stdin. Grade the transcript, not just the output - whether the skill loaded at all is the primary signal in evals 2 and 3, and whether the delivered quotes resolve is the primary signal in evals 1 and 4.
notes: Two failure modes drive this set. Over-firing: 'channel' and 'summon' are ordinary English, and a neighbouring skill often owns the task better. Quote integrity: a fluent answer in someone's voice, in quotation marks, about words they never said is the thing this skill is most prone to.

evals.name: domain-routing-without-a-name
evals.prompt: our wordpress site falls over every time we get a decent traffic spike - like 3k concurrent and it's done. we're on page caching via a plugin but object caching is off i think. who should i be listening to on this and what would they actually tell me to do first?
assertions: Consults the Domain column and routes to mark-jaquith (WordPress core, security, performance, caching, deployment) without being told a name
Does not fabricate a persona from general WordPress knowledge
Answers in Advisory voice - the prompt asks who to listen to, not for the person to speak
Every quoted string it delivers carries an attribution line naming a locatable artefact; anything unsourced is delivered as paraphrase, without quotation marks
Does not pad with generic caching advice presented as his documented position
evals.history: Tests the 'If the user asks a question without naming a persona, consult the Domain column' path. The failure to watch for is answering the WordPress question well and never routing at all.

evals.name: channel-is-ordinary-english
evals.prompt: quick one - i want to channel stderr into a file but still see it in the terminal while a long build runs. currently doing `make 2>build.log` and i'm flying blind. zsh on macos
assertions: Skill does NOT load; if it loads, the agent recognises within one step that no persona is being summoned and answers the shell question plainly
No persona voice, no italicised invocation line, no 'who would you like to summon?'
Answers the actual question (`make 2>&1 | tee build.log`, or `make 2> >(tee build.log >&2)` to keep the streams separate)
Does not offer to summon anyone as a follow-up
evals.history: Near-miss negative. 'channel' is a listed trigger verb and also the ordinary English word for redirecting a stream. Run this one 3+ times - triggering is stochastic, and a 1/3 fire rate is a different problem from 3/3.

evals.name: neighbour-skill-should-win
evals.prompt: i've got 8 quarters of revenue split across 5 product lines and i need one chart for the board deck that shows both the total trend and which line is actually carrying it. react app, happy to use recharts. what should i build?
assertions: The dataviz skill wins; summon does not fire on the presence of chart/visualisation vocabulary
If summon fires alongside, it does not take over - the answer is a chart design, not Tufte or Wattenberger speaking
No quoted string is attributed to a persona unless it carries a resolving pointer
The deliverable the user asked for (a concrete chart choice) is actually produced
evals.history: Competing-neighbour test. edward-tufte and amelia-wattenberger both sit in the dataviz domain, so summon has a real pull here and should lose. Over-steering - answering as Tufte instead of designing the chart - is the failure only this prompt catches.

evals.name: trigger-by-surname-no-verb
evals.prompt: got a 4 min product demo that drags in the middle - two talking-head segments back to back, then the screen recording. how would murch cut this? be specific about where
assertions: Reaches walter-murch despite no listed trigger verb ('summon'/'channel'/'what would X think' are all absent)
Alias matching is an exact match on a list item, not a substring search over prose
Applies documented material - the Rule of Six and its ordering - rather than generic editing advice in his voice
Any quoted string carries an attribution line with a locatable artefact; unsourced material is delivered as paraphrase
Flags extrapolation where the question outruns the dossier, rather than inventing a position
evals.history: 'How would X cut this?' is how a real user names a person without using a trigger verb. Baseline failure to watch for: answering as a generic editor, or reaching for a persona but delivering invented quotes in quotation marks.
